{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Deerskin / HDI Internet Agreement)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer-side)
**Re:** Contract review findings, verified against playbook

---

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. The document is, on its face, a revenue-share hosting and development arrangement with HDI, and it is materially incomplete on the risk-allocation provisions we would expect in any arrangement where a vendor develops, hosts and operates a customer-facing site and processes our customer data.

The most serious gap is the **complete absence of any ownership or intellectual property provision**. The Agreement addresses Content delivery, editorial control, a limited licence of our Marks to HDI and e-mail list cross-promotion, but never states who owns the Site deliverables, our Content, or the customer, user and order data generated by the Site. We have inserted a Proprietary Rights section confirming our ownership, with a licence-back in lieu of assignment offered as a landing zone given HDI bears the development cost.

Three further provisions are simply missing and each sits below even our fallback: **indemnification** (no HDI defence for third-party IP claims on a site it builds and hosts, no cover for breach of law, Content security incidents or gross negligence — walk-away territory under the rule), **limitation of liability** (both parties exposed to unlimited direct and consequential damages), and **insurance** (no cover required from a vendor processing our customer data). There is also **no exit mechanic at all** — Section 4 covers term, notice and the Termination Payment, but nothing requires HDI to return or delete our Content, user information and customer data.

On the drafted terms, the exit economics are the principal commercial problem. The Section 4.2(a) **Termination Payment** (50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000) is triggered by any Company termination, and because our fees are only 30% of Net Sales above $11,000 per month, that formula routinely exceeds a full year's fees. We have capped it at three months' fees and confirmed it is the sole liquidated amount, and separately added an express mid-term convenience right, which the Agreement currently denies us.

The Section 6.1 **exclusivity and non-compete** covenants bind us for an open-ended, auto-renewing term with elastic scope ("products substantially similar", "companies similar to") and no performance-based release. We have taken the fallback on both: the defined Deerskin Products category, 12 months, automatic termination on any HDI service level or delivery date failure, plus internal-development and acquisition carve-outs. HDI's reciprocal covenant in Section 6.3 benefits us and is untouched.

Smaller but material fixes: HDI may currently assign freely, including to a competitor (Section 10.3 is a bare successors clause); HDI's records inspection under Section 3.4 has no frequency limit; Section 9 contains no performance warranty of any kind for the design, development, hosting or operation of the Site; the Section 1.4 access rights do not extend to our affiliates; and the Section 4.1 non-renewal notice window of 90 days exceeds our 60-day ceiling.

Four rules came back clean and require no action: governing law (New York, our preferred forum, with no arbitration or foreign venue anywhere in the document), no MFN obligation burdening us, no minimum purchase or volume commitment (fees are a pure revenue share on actual Net Sales), and no non-solicitation covenant binding us.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 1.4 | No ownership/IP provision anywhere; Site deliverables, our Content and Site data unallocated. Proprietary Rights section inserted; licence-back offered as fallback. |
| 2 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 | Section 10.3 is a bare successors clause; HDI may assign freely, including to a competitor. Consent standard added at preferred level. |
| 3 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 | Section 3.4 inspection right has no frequency limit. Once-per-year cap added; other fallback terms already met or bettered (30 days' notice, HDI bears costs). |
| 4 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 5.4 | Section 10.5 selects New York law (preferred) and disclaims conflicts rules. No arbitration or foreign venue. Express exclusive venue absent — noted only. |
| 5 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 1.4 | No MFN construct anywhere. Sections 3.1–3.4 are a fixed 30% revenue share with no third-party matching obligation. |
| 6 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 1.4 | No minimum spend, take-or-pay or volume floor. Fees payable solely on actual Net Sales above $11,000/month. |
| 7 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 5.4 | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binds us; employment references are incidental only. |
| 8 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Missing | § 1.4 | No exit mechanic; Section 8 imposes no return/destruction duty and Section 10.7 is silent. New Section 4.3 inserted (6 months' assistance, 30-day data return, deletion with certification). |
| 9 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.4 | Section 9 contains only a mutual authority representation and a Globix acknowledgment; no performance warranty or remedy. Express warranty inserted (90 days services / 12 months conformance, repair-replace-refund). |
| 10 | Low | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 | Section 6.1 exclusivity runs for the open-ended auto-renewing term with elastic scope and no performance release. Fallback taken: Deerskin Products, 12 months, release on HDI failure. |
| 11 | Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless language anywhere — walk-away territory. New Section 9A inserted with four preferred claim categories and a narrow reciprocal indemnity. |
| 12 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 | No insurance obligation despite HDI hosting the Site and processing our customer data. New Section 10.9 inserted (CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' comp). |
| 13 | Low | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 | Section 4.2 Termination Payment (50% of trailing 12-month Net Sales above $800,000) routinely exceeds a year's fees. Capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount. |
| 14 | Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 | Section 1.4 access/use rights run to the Company alone, with no affiliate mechanism. Fallback proposed: affiliates on written notice, transferable to an M&A successor. |
| 15 | Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 | No cap or damages exclusion anywhere; unlimited exposure both ways. Mutual cap inserted (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000) with standard uncapped carve-outs. |
| 16 | Low | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 | Section 6.1 field-of-use restriction fails on scope, duration and carve-outs (Section 6.2 carves out only a closeout site). Fallback taken: named Deerskin Products, 12 months, internal development and acquisition carve-outs. |
| 17 | Low | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Deviation | § 1.4 | Section 4.1's 90-day non-renewal window exceeds our 60-day ceiling and the clause is silent on renewal pricing. Shortened to 30 days, with reminder and lesser-of-CPI-and-3% cap. |
| 18 | Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 1.4 | We have no mid-term convenience right, and any Company termination triggers the uncapped Section 4.2(a) payment. Fallback taken: 90 days' notice, exit payment capped at three months' Section 3.1 payments. |

---

## Walk-away items

These are the points we should not sign around:

1. **No indemnification (INDEMN, § 5.4 — missing).** The Agreement runs straight from Warranties (Section 9) into General Provisions (Section 10). HDI develops and hosts the Site, yet owes us no defence for third-party IP claims, breach of law, Content security incidents or gross negligence and wilful misconduct. The finding records this as walk-away territory under the rule. Section 9A must go in.
2. **No ownership or IP provision (IP, § 1.4 — missing).** Both the preferred and fallback positions are unmet. Our Content, Marks and Site/customer data are unprotected and could be claimed by HDI as developer and host. Either the assignment construct or the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence-back must be agreed.
3. **Uncapped exit penalty (LD / T4C, §§ 4.1–4.2).** The Termination Payment formula exceeds a year's fees while our fees are only 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month, and we have no mid-term convenience right at all. The three-month cap and the express convenience right are linked and should be treated as a single non-negotiable package.
4. **Open-ended exclusivity and non-compete (§ 6.1).** An elastic, indefinitely renewing restriction on our own commercial activity with no performance-based release is not acceptable. We can live at the fallback (Deerskin Products, 12 months, automatic release on HDI service level or delivery date failure), but not with the clause as drafted.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline.** Eighteen findings are addressed; fourteen carry proposals. The four compliant findings (GOVLAW, MFN, MINCOMMIT, NOSOLICIT) require no markup and should be flagged to the business as clean so no negotiating capital is spent there.
2. **Sequence the negotiation.** Lead with the four walk-away items (IP, indemnity, exit economics, exclusivity scope). Present limitation of liability, insurance and the transition/data-return clause as the standard package that any hosting vendor is expected to accept — all three are wholly absent rather than negotiated positions, which should make them easier to land.
3. **Signal our fallbacks early where sensible.** On IP we can accept a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Deliverables in lieu of assignment, given HDI bears the development costs. On exclusivity, non-compete, licence scope and termination for convenience we are already drafting at the fallback, and should say so.
4. **Confirm two commercial inputs with the business** before the next exchange: (a) which Company affiliates need Section 1.4 access, to support the affiliate-on-notice amendment; and (b) trailing twelve-month Net Sales, so we can quantify the current Section 4.2(a) exposure against the proposed three-month cap.
5. **Housekeeping if drafting reopens.** If Section 10.5 is touched for other reasons, add an exclusive venue sentence naming the state and federal courts in New York County. We are not redlining for this alone. Note also that Section 10.7 already lists Section 9 as surviving, so the new warranty needs no survival edit.
6. **Circulate for business sign-off** on the walk-away list before we send, so our position on those four items is firm when HDI responds."}
